first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that simplifying onboarding can improve completion, time-to-value, and durable early activation. Verifying those records is the highest-value use of the archive budget. Promotional pricing addresses competitor pressure but carries documented retention risk, conflicting with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding for self-serve SMB accounts. The closest confirmed evidence showed 13% higher completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention. Signup simplification also lifted SMB activation by 9% and qualified revenue by 4%, but its 1% retention decline warrants explicit retention guardrails and should not be generalized beyond SMB. This direction directly addresses both current declines while better supporting sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, which has known material retention risk.
